R101.note: Allowlist rejects any URI with a host and validates relative paths against a fixed set, falling back to /home; closes open redirect cleanly for this synthetic case.

R102.note: Adds server-side IsInRole("Admin") check via cascading AuthenticationState before the delete call, matching Blazor's documented pattern for event-handler authorization.

R103.note: Parameterized JNDI filter with {0} placeholder and explicit SearchControls matches the default controls the original null argument produced; correct RFC-4515-safe escaping via DirContext.search's 4-arg overload.

R104.note: Regex allowlist on pluginName fully prevents traversal by construction; the extra path.resolve/path.relative block is redundant and awkwardly written but is dead-weight, not a functional bug.

R105.note: allowed_classes restricted to ShoppingCart matches the existing instanceof check; precise fix.

R106.note: The 'recommended' Option 1 adds a findForTenantSafe() wrapper but never rewires InvoiceService/InvoiceController to call it, so the actual call path still invokes the unvalidated findForTenant() and the injection remains reachable; Option 2 (presented as an alternative) does correctly close it.

R107.note: Switches to POST + ValidateAntiForgeryToken and updates the confirm page to a token-carrying form in lockstep; standard, complete CSRF fix.

R108.note: Adds requireRole('admin') matching the exact pattern used by every sibling admin route.

R109.note: Fix references message.UserId, but ChatMessage's actual property (shown in ChatMessageStore.cs) is AuthorUserId -- this does not compile.

R110.note: Regex allowlist restricts username to safe characters before concatenation, structurally excluding all LDAP metacharacters used in the filter.

R111.note: snprintf with explicit capacity checks preserves the "AUDIT user:action" format and returns -1 (reject, not truncate) exactly per the stated contract.

R112.note: htmlspecialchars with ENT_QUOTES at the echo sink; straightforward correct fix.

R113.note: Replacement InvoiceMapper.findForTenant drops the sort parameter, but InvoiceService.listInvoices (unchanged) still calls the two-arg overload -- the codebase would not compile as delivered. Also permanently loses legitimate sort combinations (e.g. status desc, total_cents asc) not covered by the four canned queries.

R114.note: Replacing the shell-out with archive/tar eliminates the injection entirely and preserves the text/plain listing format, but the write-up itself admits ctx is no longer used for cancellation, dropping the contract's explicit 'continues using the request context for cancellation' requirement.

R115.note: Uses the file-type-detected extension instead of the client-supplied one; closes the extension/content mismatch cleanly.

R116.note: Eliminates the shell entirely via System.Net.NetworkInformation.Ping, closing CWE-78 completely, but silently changes observable output: original returned PowerShell's multi-line Test-Connection -Count 4 report, new code returns a single custom-formatted line from one ping.Send() call -- not disclosed as a behavior change.

R117.note: finfo-based content-type allowlist plus randomized filename with mapped extension; solid, complete fix.

R118.note: csrf-csrf double-submit token is an appropriate mechanism, but registerTransferRoutes now takes doubleCsrfProtection as a required parameter with no default, so any unmodified caller breaks route registration; also removes the origin check without demonstrating that the new middleware's failure path actually returns the contract-required 403 JSON shape.

R119.note: htmlspecialchars(ENT_QUOTES) applied to both interpolated fields; correct.

R120.note: Allowlist of sort strings including the default 'created_at desc'; throws on invalid input rather than passing tainted SQL through orderByRaw.

R121.note: Bounds check against calibrationTable.size() before the write; minimal, correct.

R122.note: Correctly separates the two output contexts: sanitized HTML for the body, extracted+quote-escaped plain text for the title attribute, matching the stated dual-context contract.

R123.note: Encodes ASCII control range, DEL, and Unicode line/paragraph separators before interpolation; closes CRLF log injection.

R124.note: Upload-side fix (content sniffing, random filename) is solid, but the contract explicitly requires the read path (avatar_lookup.go's ReadAvatarBytes) be updated in step -- that file is never touched; the write-up only states in prose that callers 'must now pass the generated filename,' which is a disclosed but unfulfilled requirement, not an actual fix.

R125.note: strrchr-based true-extension check plus randomized filename closes the double-extension bypass; standard, complete fix.

R126.note: The escapeControlCharacters regex literals for U+0085/U+2028/U+2029 contain raw Unicode line-terminator characters embedded directly in the source; verified with node that this throws 'SyntaxError: Invalid regular expression: missing /' -- the file does not parse.

R127.note: resize(count) correctly fixes the reported OOB write into packet, but the contract explicitly requires rejecting/reporting counts larger than fields.size(); the fix adds no such check, so fields[i] silently reads out of bounds when count > fields.size(), which is exactly the scenario the contract says must not be silently truncated/allowed.

R128.note: Replaces ECB with AES-GCM, prepending a fresh nonce; the only observable change (nonce+ciphertext instead of bare ciphertext) is stated plainly and the endpoint still succeeds for every caller.

R129.note: SecureRandom replaces attacker-seedable Random; removing the seed parameter is the necessary fix, not a legitimate feature loss.

R130.note: Bypassing self-invocation by calling the repository directly correctly closes the AOP-proxy bypass, but adding @PreAuthorize("hasRole('ADMIN')") to processMonthEndCleanup -- described as a 'nightly batch job entry point' -- risks throwing AccessDeniedException when the scheduler invokes it without an authenticated ADMIN principal in context; this risk is not discussed.

R131.note: Callback-based setTimeout instead of a spliced eval string; eliminates code injection entirely, response body unchanged.

R132.note: Minimal, correct: flips the explicit setSecure(false) to true.

R133.note: Uses Express's root option in sendFile(), the idiomatic confinement mechanism for this sink.

R134.note: log/slog escapes control characters in attribute values in both its text and JSON encodings (verified against slog's quoting behavior); HTTP response path is untouched, only internal log formatting changes.

R135.note: firebase/jwt's JWT::decode enforces signature verification and returns null on failure, correctly closing the forgery vector; however the code falls back to a hardcoded default secret ('your-secret-key') when JWT_SECRET is unset, a live weakness if deployed without setting the env var, and this risk is only mentioned as an aside rather than guarded against in code.

R136.note: session_regenerate_id() before writing authenticated session state; default (keeps old session data) matches the write-up's own description and preserves the immediate _SESSION writes.

R137.note: execFile with domain as a separate array argument removes shell interpretation entirely; response handling unchanged.

R138.note: unserialize(..., ['allowed_classes'=>false]) correctly blocks gadget-chain instantiation for legacy rows, but the contract explicitly requires loadCart to also return correct contents for rows written after the migration (now JSON) -- unserialize() on a JSON string returns false, which violates the declared ': array' return type and loses that user's cart; the write-up explicitly (and incorrectly) argues this JSON path is unnecessary.

R139.note: require_http_methods(['POST']) plus Django's built-in CSRF middleware; correct, standard fix, template update disclosed.

R140.note: Resource-based ownership check via IAuthorizationService correctly closes the missing-authorization vector, but on failure it returns Forbid() (403) rather than the contract's explicit requirement that 'unauthorized invoice IDs do not reveal more than the original not-found path' -- distinguishing 403-exists-but-forbidden from 404-not-found is exactly the enumeration oracle the contract prohibits, and the write-up's explanation argues for this choice directly against the stated contract.
